thread:
acme_integration: Hey team — since the private deployment yesterday we're getting failures when our service calls the KMS key lookup. Error in prod logs: "dial tcp: lookup kms.internal on 10.0.0.2:53: no such host" and then a TLS handshake timeout. Started around 09:12 UTC. Any ideas?

emma_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact client error and the time-range? Is this only from one AZ/bastion?

acme_integration: Sure. From our app logs (09:11:58): 
```
error: rpc.key.lookup failed: context deadline exceeded
cause: dial tcp 10.1.5.12:443: i/o timeout
root: lookup kms.internal on 10.0.0.2:53: no such host
```
This happens from all pods in the VPC subnet us-east-2a. We did a config change to route egress through a customer gateway last night.

javier_infra: Quick guess: DNS resolution to the internal KMS hostname is failing because your egress path is using an upstream resolver that doesn't know the private zone. Can you run these from a failing pod/bastion?
```
dig @10.0.0.2 kms.internal +short
dig @8.8.8.8 kms.internal +short
curl -v https://10.1.5.12/health --connect-timeout 5
```

acme_integration: Running those now. Output:
```
$ dig @10.0.0.2 kms.internal +short
; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
$ dig @8.8.8.8 kms.internal +short
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @8.8.8.8 kms.internal +short
; 8.8.8.8 can't find kms.internal: NXDOMAIN
$ curl -v https://10.1.5.12/health --connect-timeout 5
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.1.5.12 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to 10.1.5.12 port 443: Operation timed out
```

emma_support: That confirms two issues: 1) your DNS resolver (10.0.0.2) is not responding over the new egress path, and 2) direct TCP to the KMS IP is timing out. Likely an egress firewall/NAT problem on the gateway.

maya_sre: Also check for reverse path filtering or SNAT. If your gateway is doing SNAT to a set of ephemeral IPs not whitelisted by the KMS side, the remote may be dropping connections. Can you run a traceroute and tcpdump (on the gateway) while making a test request?

javier_infra: For quick repro steps and a temporary workaround: 1) from bastion add an /etc/hosts entry mapping kms.internal -> 10.1.5.12 and retry to confirm it's DNS-only. 2) ensure the gateway allows outbound TCP/443 to 10.1.5.0/24 and allows UDP/53 to your DNS resolver (10.0.0.2).

acme_integration: I added the hosts entry on the bastion and curl to 10.1.5.12 now returns HTTP/1.1 200 OK for /health. So DNS is the main blocker. But pods still fail because they use the cluster DNS server.

emma_support: Good confirmation. Next steps: please work with your network team to allow DNS traffic from the cluster DNS (ip 10.0.0.3?) to your resolver at 10.0.0.2 over UDP/TCP 53 across the new egress path. If your gateway performs DNS forwarding, make sure it preserves source IPs or adjust the KMS allowlist accordingly.

acme_integration: One more weirdness — we saw intermittent TLS resets earlier: "tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate". Could that be certificate pinning on the KMS side?

maya_sre: That sounds like either a proxy doing TLS termination (replace cert) or a mismatched SNI. Verify your client is sending the SNI hostname 'kms.internal' and not the IP. Example test: 
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.1.5.12:443 -servername kms.internal -showcerts
```
If the cert presented does not match kms.internal, the handshake will fail.

acme_integration: Ran the openssl test — cert CN is kms.internal and chain looks fine when connecting directly. So the TLS failures were probably the result of a misrouted flow hitting a middlebox without the right SNI.

javier_infra: Action items from infra side:
- Confirm egress NAT preserves source IPs or update KMS allowlist to include the NAT pool.
- Allow UDP/TCP 53 to 10.0.0.2 from cluster DNS IPs.
- Ensure any HTTP/TLS proxy on the gateway passes SNI through (no TLS termination).
We can open a ticket with the on-call network vendor if you share traceroute/tcpdump output.

emma_support: I'll create an internal escalation with SRE and Networking and loop in the customer's network team. For now your workaround (hosts entry on bastion) can unblock some ops, but not pods. ETA for networking review: 2 hours.

ops-bot: Created internal incident INC-2025-3247 and assigned to eng-infra oncall.

acme_integration: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. We'll gather tcpdump/traceroute and send to the ticket. Keep me posted on any firewall/NAT config changes we should expect. :thumbsup:

emma_support: Will do. If you can, please capture one failing pod's /var/log/syslog and the kube-proxy logs for the time window 09:10–09:20 UTC, that'll help trace the NAT path.

acme_integration: Will attach those to INC-2025-3247 within the hour.
